question: Can I bring my dog into the kitchen?
answer: I could not find an answer to this in the trusted food-safety documents (FDA Food Code excerpts, Hawaii food-safety rules, and Pacific Market Cafe SOPs). Please check with your manager or the source documents directly.

passages.doc: SOP-03 — Employee Illness Reporting (Pacific Market Cafe)
passages.heading: Reportable diagnoses
passages.text:
Reportable diagnoses
vomiting, diarrhea, or jaundice must report it to the
manager on duty and may not work with food. Employees with vomiting or
diarrhea may return only after being symptom-free for at least 48 hours.
A diagnosis of Norovirus, Salmonella, Shigella, E. coli (STEC), or
Hepatitis A must be reported to the manager, who reports it to the local
health department. These employees are excluded from the establishment.

passages.doc: SOP-03 — Employee Illness Reporting (Pacific Market Cafe)
passages.heading: Corrective action
passages.text:
Corrective action
required by the health department, written medical clearance. Return
after vomiting or diarrhea without a diagnosis requires the full 48
symptom-free hours and the approval of the manager on duty.
Send home any employee who reports or shows a symptom requiring exclusion,
and reassign their station. Discard any food they may have contaminated, and
clean and sanitize the surfaces and equipment they used. Retrain any
employee who worked a shift without reporting a symptom requiring exclusion.

passages.doc: FDA Food Code §4-501 — Cleaning and Sanitizing
passages.heading: Wiping cloths
passages.text:
Wiping cloths
and utensils in continuous use with TCS food must be
cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours. Surfaces must be washed,
rinsed, and sanitized — in that order — after each use with raw animal food.
In-use wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution at the proper
concentration between uses, never left on counters.

passages.doc: SOP-01 — Receiving and Storage (Pacific Market Cafe)
passages.heading: Cold storage order
passages.text:
Cold storage order
carton, and no other sign of thawing and refreezing.

Inspect the truck for cleanliness and odor, check the integrity of the
packaging, and check the use-by dates on milk, eggs, and other perishables.
Store food in the walk-in from top shelf to bottom shelf in this order:
ready-to-eat foods, whole cuts of beef and pork, ground meats, and raw
poultry on the bottom shelf. The order follows cooking temperature — the
food that needs the highest cooking temperature sits lowest, so nothing can
drip onto a food that will be cooked to a lower temperature or eaten as is.
Never store raw animal foods above ready-to-eat foods.
